statement: For any binary operation add on the real numbers, the construction repeatedly splits the current list into a first part of ceiling half its length and a remaining part, combines corresponding entries with add, and carries any unmatched entry forward. It performs d rounds, where d is the least natural number with the original length at most 2^d, then returns the first remaining value, defaulting to zero. For a nonempty list the supplied structural theorem identifies this result with evaluation of a full binary tree of height exactly d whose real leaf labels form a permutation of the input. Under the stated uniform relative rounding model, u >= 0, and d*u < 1, the supplied error theorem represents that actual result as the exact sum of additively perturbed original entries, with each perturbation bounded by (d*u)/(1-d*u) times the magnitude of its entry. The depth theorem characterizes d for all natural input lengths, including zero.

targets.name: Bhola.theorem_3_1_global
targets.statement: For every function add: R x R -> R and every finite list xs of real numbers with xs != [], and for every implicitly quantified real u, assume 0 <= u, and assume that for all a,b in R there exists a real delta with |delta| <= u and add(a,b) = (a+b)*(1+delta). Write n = length(xs), d = Bhola.depth(n), and x_i = xs[i] for i in Fin(n) = {0,...,n-1}. Also assume (d cast to R)*u < 1. Then there exists a function Delta: Fin(n) -> R such that Bhola.algorithm(add,xs) = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (x_i + Delta(i)) and, for every i in Fin(n), |Delta(i)| <= Bhola.gamma(d,u)*|x_i|, where Bhola.gamma(d,u) = ((d cast to R)*u)/(1-(d cast to R)*u). The sum uses ordinary exact real addition; Delta(i) is an additive perturbation of the original entry. The algorithm here is precisely the split-and-pair construction described below, run for d rounds. The strict inequality and u >= 0 make the denominator positive.

targets.name: Bhola.algorithm1_spec
targets.statement: For every function add: R x R -> R and every finite nonempty list xs of real numbers, put n = length(xs) and d = Bhola.depth(n). There exists a finite tree t built from leaf(a), a in R, and node(left,right), such that all four properties hold: (1) Bhola.stagesValues(add,d,xs) is the singleton list [eval_add(t)]; (2) leaves(t) is a permutation of xs, preserving multiplicities; (3) height(t) = d; and (4) Bhola.algorithm(add,xs) = eval_add(t). Here eval_add(leaf(a)) = a and eval_add(node(s,t)) = add(eval_add(s),eval_add(t)); leaves(leaf(a)) = [a] and leaves(node(s,t)) is leaves(s) followed by leaves(t); height(leaf(a)) = 0 and height(node(s,t)) = max(height(s),height(t))+1. No rounding, associativity, commutativity, or other hypothesis on add is present. The tree witnesses the actual d-round computation; the statement requires only a permutation of input leaves, not equality to their original order.

targets.name: Bhola.depth_spec
targets.statement: For all natural numbers n and k (including zero), Bhola.depth(n) <= k if and only if n <= 2^k, with the power and inequalities in the natural numbers. The supplied definition is Bhola.depth(n) = Nat.clog(2,n); the equivalence characterizes it as the least nonnegative integer k with n <= 2^k. Thus depth(0) = depth(1) = 0, and for n >= 1 it is the ceiling of log base 2 of n. Applied to n = length(xs), this is the number of rounds used by Bhola.algorithm and the exact height in Bhola.algorithm1_spec, and it supplies d in the error bound of Bhola.theorem_3_1_global.

constructions.name: Bhola.algorithm
constructions.description: Domain: an arbitrary function add: R x R -> R and a finite real list xs. Let n = length(xs) and d = Bhola.depth(n) = Nat.clog(2,n), equivalently the least natural d with n <= 2^d by Bhola.depth_spec. Return the head of Bhola.stagesValues(add,d,xs), using the real number 0 if that list is empty. In particular the empty input returns 0 and a singleton [a] returns a. On nonempty input Bhola.algorithm1_spec states that the final list is a singleton and its element is evaluation using add of a tree with input leaves up to permutation and height d. The operation is unrestricted in the definition; it is subject to a rounding model only in the error theorem.

constructions.name: Bhola.stagesValues
constructions.description: Domain: add: R x R -> R, a natural round count k, and a finite real list xs. Define stagesValues(add,0,xs) = xs and stagesValues(add,k+1,xs) = stagesValues(add,k,roundValues(add,xs)). Thus it iterates roundValues exactly k times, recomputing the split from the current list at each round. Empty lists stay empty and singleton lists stay unchanged. The algorithm chooses k = depth(length(xs)); the structural theorem identifies the resulting singleton for nonempty input, and the error theorem bounds its element.

constructions.name: Bhola.roundValues
constructions.description: Domain: add: R x R -> R and a finite real list xs. Set n = length(xs) and h = floor((n+1)/2) = ceiling(n/2), using natural-number division. Return pairValues(add,take(h,xs),drop(h,xs)). In zero-based indices, if n = 2m the output is [add(x_0,x_m), ..., add(x_{m-1},x_{2m-1})]; if n = 2m+1 it is [add(x_0,x_{m+1}), ..., add(x_{m-1},x_{2m}), x_m]. A range with no indices contributes no entries: the empty list returns [] and [x_0] returns [x_0]. Thus one round pairs corresponding positions across the two parts, and for odd length places the unpaired final entry of the first part at the end. The output length is ceiling(n/2). These are the rounds iterated by stagesValues.

constructions.name: Bhola.pairValues
constructions.description: Domain: add: R x R -> R and two finite real lists xs, ys. Recursively, pairValues(add,[],ys) = ys; pairValues(add,xs,[]) = xs; and pairValues(add,a::xs,b::ys) = add(a,b)::pairValues(add,xs,ys), where :: prepends a list entry. Equivalently, apply add to corresponding entries up to the shorter length, then append the unchanged remaining suffix of the longer list. The output length is max(length(xs),length(ys)); no neutral value or extra call to add is used for unmatched entries. roundValues supplies the first and second parts of its current list to this function.

assumptions: R denotes the real numbers; lists are finite and ordered, natural numbers include zero, and Fin(n) indexes list entries from 0 to n-1. Natural depths are cast to real numbers in products with u.

All four listed constructions are defined for every binary real function add and every list in their stated domains; stagesValues additionally takes any natural round count. No algebraic or numerical restriction on add is implicit.
Bhola.algorithm1_spec assumes only that its real input list is nonempty, with universal quantification over add and the list.

Bhola.theorem_3_1_global universally quantifies add and the nonempty real input list, and implicitly universally quantifies the real parameter u. Its hypotheses are 0 <= u, Bhola.RoundingModel(add,u), and depth(length(xs))*u < 1.

Bhola.RoundingModel(add,u) means: for every pair a,b of real numbers, there exists a real delta, allowed to depend on a and b, satisfying |delta| <= u and add(a,b) = (a+b)*(1+delta). It is a condition on all real arguments, not only arguments reached by the construction.

Bhola.depth_spec has no hypotheses beyond n,k being natural numbers. Neither structural theorem requires the rounding model or the bounds on u. The error theorem imposes no sign restriction on input entries and no additional restriction such as u < 1.
